topPRs.title: fix: preserve complete evidence and remove dormant duplicate code
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Closes #30553, #30554, #30555, #30556, #30558. Implements two bounded consolidation/removal slices of #30125; does not close that broader tracker.

This cleanup preserves complete Git and scheduled-event evidence, rejects invalid analysis merges, removes a queue listener leak, makes widget certification fail when execution fails, consolidates connector-token encryption, and deletes an unused voice-profile prototype. The changes were selected from a parallel source/caller audit and independently reviewed across lanes.

- [x] Targets `develop`; rebased on `f3017932d3501c1e13b78fa248c6f074dd5e5c88` with zero conflicts.
- [x] Bun 1.3.14 install and Node 24.15.0 verification run after sync.
- [x] Concrete before/after examples and local validation are recorded below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Latest fetched develop base is `f3017932d3501c1e13b78fa248c6f074dd5e5c88`.
- [x] Post-sync `bun run verify` passes; see final exact-head ledger below.

# Risks

Medium. Invalid or incomplete Git output now throws; scheduled event data must be complete plain JSON rather than relying on lossy JavaScript conversions. Existing expected non-repository/unborn states and absent optional event payloads remain supported. The queue schema/locking and token key paths/envelope remain unchanged. No deployed renderer or native bridge implementation changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces duplicate synchronous/shell Git readers with one complete async reader; uses NUL-delimited filename protocols. A real 10.7 MB change previously lost its final marker while reporting `truncated:false`; Unicode paths previously pointed to nonexistent files.
- Validates analysis document identity and results-map shape before merging. Arrays and mismatched subjects fail without replacing original bytes; arbitrary analyzer IDs are stored as own data properties.
- Disposes the idle worker's abort listener on normal timer expiry and handles already-aborted signals immediately.
- Replaces two 16,000-character event-payload cutoff helpers with a scheduling-owned JSON boundary; persistence, retry/escalation and final prompt assembly retain complete event data. Unsupported data fails before task claim.
- Makes widget execution errors nonzero, clears old output, and reuses local fixture/Tailwind helpers instead of a CDN and fixed wait. Completed widget findings retain the existing `FAIL_ON_VIOLATIONS` policy.
- Moves byte-identical finance/health token encryption into a Node-only shared subpath, retaining plugin compatibility exports and old envelopes.
- Removes 13 unregistered/unexported voice-profile prototype files, including fabricated diarization and a 617-line self-contained role “integration” suite. Live voice-profile persistence remains in local-inference.

## What kind of change is this?

Behavioral bug fixes, consolidation, and removal of unused code. 44 files; net 749 lines removed including tests and compatibility adapters.

# Documentation changes needed?

Updated shared subpath documentation and paired UI CLAUDE/AGENTS instructions. Guide parity passes. The detailed audit and remaining candidates are retained as local review artifacts, not committed evidence.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

Review each issue's observable acceptance result, then the complete-diff/payload regressions, real filesystem merge tests, worker idle-loop tests, and real certification subprocess failures. Independent review covered Git capture (lead), evidence/queue (product lane), widget runner (runtime lane), and scheduling/crypto (cloud lane). Scheduling's first draft was corrected after independent review identified Maps/Sets that JSON would silently discard.

## Detailed testing steps

Run the owning package test scripts and root `bun run verify` using the pinned runtimes. Local terminal results:

| Package/lane | Passed | Existing skips |
|---|---:|---:|
| Evidence | 529 | 2 live-only files |
| Agent orchestrator | 3,115 | 10 tests |
| Shared | 2,847 | 0 |
| Finances | 188 | 0 |
| Health | 199 | 4 tests |
| Scheduling | 638 | 0 |
| Personal assistant | 2,492 | 6 tests |
| UI | 13,500 | 7 tests |
| App-core Vitest | 4,461 | 25 tests |
| App-core script suites | 74 Node + 21 Bun | 0 |

A workflow-only develop update was rebased after the package suites completed. Git tree IDs prove all nine affected package trees are identical to the tested revision; the two changed base workflow suites additionally passed 28 tests. Root verification was rerun on the rebased head.

All owning-package typechecks/lint and required build dependencies pass through root verification. Chromium and WebKit each certified 2/2 widget fixtures (tap-target/scroll dimensions), with no console errors; screenshots were inspected. This is not a whole-app visual audit.

topPRs.title: fix(i18n): stop the action-search regen from evicting committed locale terms
topPRs.author: attentionhead
topPRs.body:
# What

Regenerating the action-search keywords **destroys committed translations**. Running the repo's own `generate:action-search-keywords` on current `develop` adds the 4 missing entries it should — and silently drops **16 committed terms across 15 key/locale pairs**:

| entry | locale | term lost |
|---|---|---|
| `action.file.request` | es / ko / pt / tl / vi / zh-CN | `escribir archivo`, `쓰기 파일`, `escrever arquivo`, `isulat file`, `viết tệp`, `写入 文件` |
| `action.runtimes.request` | es / ko / pt / tl / vi / zh-CN | `token`, `토큰`, `token`, `token`, `tao`, `代币` + `令牌` |
| `action.views.request` | ko / tl / zh-CN | `쓰기`, `isulat`, `写入` |

`base` loses nothing — #22402's pinning from f0d4c39d9 works, but **only for `base`**. Every loss is in a locale.

So "the artifact is stale" was not something you could fix by running the generator. That's what this PR fixes first.

# Two independent causes

**1. `buildLocaleTerms` translated `base.slice(0, 64)`** — a positional window over an alphabetically sorted, *growing* list. In `action.file.request`, `write file` sat at base index 59; the regen's new terms pushed it to 67, out of the window, so all six of its localized forms stopped being derivable. Nothing about term 65 makes it less worth translating than term 64 — `64` was the only bare numeric limit in the file (`BASE_LIMIT`/`LOCALE_LIMIT` are named constants) and had no comment. **10 of the 16 losses come from this, all of them below the locale cap.**

**2. The locale lists never pinned `existing[locale]`.** `base` uses `limitTermsPinned`; each locale used plain `limitTerms`, so committed terms were re-scored against fresh candidates and evicted at `LOCALE_LIMIT`. This is precisely the bug f0d4c39d9 describes, on the code path it didn't cover. **The remaining 6 losses, all at the 48-term cap.**

# The change

```js
-  for (const term of base.slice(0, 64)) {
+  for (const term of base) {
```
```js
-    const deduped = limitTerms(dedupeTerms(terms), LOCALE_LIMIT);
+    const deduped = limitTermsPinned(
+      dedupeTerms(arrayValue(existing[locale])),
+      dedupeTerms(terms),
+      LOCALE_LIMIT,
+    );
```

That was `limitTerms`' last caller, so it's removed (biome flagged it).

# Both edits are load-bearing, and the window fix is *not* safe alone

| variant | committed terms lost | terms gained |
|---|---|---|
| `develop` (neither) | **16** | +81 |
| window fix only | **129** | +287 |
| pin fix only | **0** | +76 |
| **both (this PR)** | **0** | **+158** |

Translating all of `base` floods the 48-slot candidate list, so on its own it makes eviction **eight times worse**. It's only safe once the committed terms are pinned. Applied together the regen becomes purely additive: **0 lost, +158 gained, 4 entries added, 0 removed.**

I'll flag a claim I had to drop: I first justified the window fix by arguing the new `action.channelRecap.request` (base length 68) would ship with a truncated translation set. Measured, it has 140 localized terms in all four variants — that argument was wrong. The window fix earns its place on different evidence: **+82 localized terms across 9 entries** (`browser`, `liquidity`, `logs`, `oauth`, `payment`, `room`, `scheduledTasks`, `wallet`, …), with none removed.

# The 4 entries the regen adds

All four actions are shipped and had **no search keywords in any of the 7 locales**:

| action | defined at |
|---|---|
| `CALCULATE` | `packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/actions/calculate.ts:247` |
| `CHANNEL_RECAP` | `packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/actions/channel-recap.ts:96` |
| `FAMILY_WORKFLOWS` | `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/family-workflows.ts:14` |
| `OWNER_AGREEMENT_KNOWLEDGE` | `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/agreement-knowledge.ts:59` |

# Why not `action-search-overrides.keywords.json`

I checked whether the curated terms belong in the overrides file instead. `generate-keywords.mjs` merges every `*.keywords.json` in the directory, so that would work mechanically — but overrides holds one entry of hand-authored phrasing the audit cannot derive (`server template`, `guild management`, …), and none of the lost terms. These terms *are* dictionary-derived generator output; f0d4c39d9 chose to pin rather than relocate them for exactly this reason, and this follows that precedent.

# Verification

- `node packages/scripts/generate-action-search-keywords.mjs` → deterministic; **generate + biome format is byte-idempotent**.
- Set-diff of every entry × `base` + 6 locales vs the committed artifact: **0 terms lost**, +158 gained, 151 → 155 entries, 0 entries removed.
- `bunx vitest run packages/core/src/i18n/action-search-keywords.test.ts` → **15 passed**.
- `bun run --cwd packages/shared typecheck` and `--cwd packages/core typecheck` → exit 0, 0 `error TS`.
- `node packages/shared/scripts/generate-keywords.mjs` (the second half of the npm script) → clean.
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check` on both changed files → clean; `node --check` on the generator → clean.

# Out of scope, worth a follow-up

Nothing in CI runs this generator or asserts the artifact is current, which is how 4 shipped actions went keyword-less and why the eviction went unnoticed. A staleness gate is a separate change — and it should not land before this one, since on `develop` such a gate would demand a regeneration that destroys translations.

topPRs.title: fix(agent): stop a damaged tool-cache row from failing the tool call
topPRs.author: attentionhead
topPRs.body:
## The bug

`DiskStore.read` trusted its own state directory:

```ts
const raw = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as ToolCacheEntry;
if (parsed.key !== key) return undefined;
return parsed;
```

No error handling, and an unvalidated cast on bytes this process did not write.

`ToolCallCache.run` calls that synchronously, *before* the executor:

```ts
const hit = this.getByKey(descriptor, cacheKey);   // -> disk.read(key)
if (hit && shouldCache(hit.output)) return hit.output;
```

So a malformed row does not degrade to a cache miss. It throws out of `run`
and **the tool never runs at all**. That contradicts the contract stated a few
lines away in `keyFor`, on the sibling failure path:

> error-policy:J7 the cache is optional degradation, not the tool call

I confirmed it by writing a truncated row and calling `run`:

| on-disk bytes | result | executor calls |
|---|---|---|
| `{"key":"…","toolName":"web_search"` | throws `SyntaxError` | **0** |
| `null` | throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'key')` | **0** |

And it is permanent. The read path never rewrote or removed the row it
rejected, so the same key fails on every later call — in this process and in
every future one — until someone deletes the state directory by hand:

```
attempt 1: threw SyntaxError
attempt 2: threw SyntaxError
poisoned file still present: true
```

This needs no attacker. `write` called `writeFileSync` straight onto the live
path, with no temp-and-rename, so a crash, a signal or a full disk mid-write
leaves exactly that partial file.

## A quieter consequence of the same cast

`getByKey` tests `candidate.expiresAt <= this.now()`. When the field is absent
that is `undefined <= now`, which is `false` — so the row reads as *not yet
expired at every clock value*. A row carrying no expiry is served forever and
the tool it caches never runs again. With a 1 s TTL and `now() = 1e15`:

```
served: "STALE"   executor calls: 0
```

I checked two adjacent shapes that looked equally suspect and they are fine —
a string `expiresAt` coerces and does expire, and a row with no `output` field
misses — so this is the one field where absence is silently wrong rather than
loud.

## The fix

- **`read` validates instead of casting.** A new `isStoredEntry` type guard
  checks every field the read path or `getByKey` goes on to *compare*. Any
  failure — unparseable, unreadable, non-object, or non-conforming — is a miss
  that **also evicts the file**, so the key self-heals on the next call.
- **`write` publishes atomically** through a uniquely-named temp file plus
  `rename`, so a crash cannot produce the partial row in the first place.
- **Neither method throws.** Two holes I found while auditing my own patch:
  - If `<key>.json` is a *directory*, `readFileSync` raises `EISDIR` and the
    eviction's non-recursive `rmSync` then throws too. Eviction is now
    best-effort.
  - `disk.write` runs inside `run`'s `.then`, **after the tool has already
    returned**, so a raised `ENOSPC`/`EACCES` rejects a promise whose tool
    succeeded and discards the result. `write` now logs and continues uncached.

`output` presence is checked with `in`, not truthiness, because `null`, `0` and
`false` are all valid `ToolOutput` values.

## What I deliberately did not change

- **`output` shape is not validated.** That would mean a deep walk of untrusted
  data, which `isRedactionDegraded` here and `shouldCache` in `run` already
  perform on the way out. Presence only.
- **The two traversals in `key.ts` and `bounded-walk.ts` stay separate.** The
  header comment explains why at length; nothing here needs them merged.
- **`invalidate(toolName, argHash)` does not verify that the entry's `toolName`
  matches** before deleting by hash, so `invalidate("a", hashOfB)` drops B's
  row. Both callers pass a hash they just derived from that same descriptor, so
  it is unreachable today — noting it rather than widening the diff.

## Tests

21 added, and the pinning tests updated.

- `disk-store.test.ts`: two tables — 6 malformed-bytes cases (truncated, empty,
  non-JSON, `null`, `[]`, bare number) and 8 non-conforming-shape cases — each
  asserting **miss *and* eviction**; the not-a-regular-file case; a swallowed
  publish failure leaving no temp residue.
- `cache.test.ts`: the tool runs instead of the call failing; the key self-heals
  so a second call is a hit; a no-expiry row is not served; a successful tool
  result survives a failed disk write.
- **Liveness control**: a conforming row whose `output` is `null`, `0`, `false`,
  `""`, `[]` or `{}` is still served. Without it, every "reads as a miss"
  assertion above would pass just as well if the validator rejected everything.

Two existing tests pinned the old behaviour — `throws when the on-disk row is
not JSON`, and a key-mismatch case asserting `existsSync(file)` stays `true`.
Both come from d2cdce0d56 *"test(agent): cover disk-store (#25621)"*, a coverage
commit, with no stated rationale; they recorded what the code did rather than a
designed contract, and they contradict error-policy:J7. Updated in place rather
than dropped, so the contract change is visible in the diff.

**Ablation** — reverting only `disk-store.ts` to `develop` and re-running:

```
Tests  21 failed | 220 passed (241)
```

Restored: `241 passed`. `biome check` clean; `tsc --noEmit -p packages/agent`
clean.

The wider `packages/agent/src/runtime` suite has 14 pre-existing red files on
`develop` locally (cloud-config, vault, wallet, plugin-resolver). None of them
reference `ToolCallCache` or `DiskStore`, `DiskStore` has no consumers outside
this directory, and I reproduced one of them (`plugin-resolver-preflight`) on a
clean `develop` checkout — so they are unrelated to this change rather than
something it introduced.
